title: The Heartbreak of Immigration Reform, with Esther Olavarria
description: Everyone knows that our immigration system is broken, so why hasn’t Congress fixed it for over 35 years? What you may not know is how close we came to comprehensive immigration reform – not once, not twice, but four times. Esther Olavarria was one of the foremost people working behind the scenes to make it happen, first as a staffer to Senator Ted Kennedy and later as a senior official under President Obama. This is her eyewitness account – of hope and despair, war rooms and whip counts, and honest answers on why it’s so hard for Congress to get the job done.

title: Biden and the Border (Part 2), with Charanya Krishnaswami
description: You don’t serve four years as a senior official in Biden’s Department of Homeland Security without seeing some things. This episode is Part 2 of Charanya Krishnaswami’s never-before-told story, walking us through the unprecedented border of crossings in 2023 and the misunderstood reasons those numbers dropped in 2024 – far too late for political redemption. Along the way, we call out some ugly racism on the Democratic side of the aisle, lament the futility of Congress, and conclude with Charanya’s clear-eyed border plan for the next President.

title: Biden and the Border (Part 1), with Charanya Krishnaswami
description: Nobody’s happy with how the Biden administration handled the U.S./Mexico border, but it’s hard to find an honest reckoning. That’s why you need to hear the story of Charanya Krishnaswami, a senior advisor at the Department of Homeland Security during all four of those tumultuous years. She’s brilliant, insightful, and even hilarious – all while pulling back the curtain on how so many smart people struggled to make good decisions. This episode is Part 1 of Charanya’s story, starting on day one of the Biden administration and taking us through the mounting panic of the second year…

title: The Birth of the Department of Homeland Security
description: After 9/11, the U.S. government undertook the largest federal reorganization since the creation of the Pentagon. The result was DHS — a sprawling mega-agency that absorbed immigration functions from three different departments. How did this reshuffling shape the immigration system we have today, and what did we lose in the process?
image_alt: Protesters with Never Again signs being detained by police at an immigration demonstration
transcript:
Claire Trickler-McNulty: Welcome back to The Melting Pod. Today we’re talking about something that fundamentally reshaped how America handles immigration — the creation of the Department of Homeland Security.

Doug Rand: Yeah, and I think most people don’t realize that before 2003, there was no DHS. Immigration was handled by the Immigration and Naturalization Service — the INS — which sat inside the Department of Justice.

Amanda Baran: And the INS was this fascinating, deeply dysfunctional agency that was responsible for both welcoming immigrants and deporting them. It was like having the same person be your defense attorney and the prosecutor.

Claire: Which is exactly why Congress decided to blow it up after 9/11. But the story of how DHS came together is really a story about the politics of fear, bureaucratic turf wars, and some genuinely consequential decisions made under enormous time pressure.

Doug: Let’s bring in our guest. Michael Chen served in senior roles at both the old INS and the new DHS during the transition. Michael, take us back to that moment…

[Transcript continues…]

title: The Rise and Fall of Comprehensive Immigration Reform
description: For decades, “comprehensive immigration reform” was the holy grail of immigration policy. From Reagan’s 1986 amnesty to the Gang of Eight, we trace how the grand bargain kept almost happening — and why it keeps falling apart.
image_alt: Two women wearing American flag headscarves sharing a moment of solidarity at a march

title: How Asylum and the Border Took Over American Politics
description: Asylum wasn’t always front-page news. We unpack how a legal protection created after World War II became the most politically explosive word in immigration — and what the current crackdown means for people fleeing danger.

title: Welcome to The Melting Pod
description: The Melting Pod brings you stories of our dysfunctional immigration system, and where we go from here. In this inaugural episode, Claire reveals how everything going on with ICE is even worse than it looks; Amanda explains how Trump is de-legalizing millions of people who thought they were protected; and Doug shatters any remaining illusions that MAGA is okay with legal immigrants. Plus we introduce ourselves, drag the New York Times a bit, and give you a few things to be hopeful about in 2026. Join us!
summary:
The Melting Pod brings you stories of our dysfunctional immigration system, and where we go from here.

In this inaugural episode, Claire reveals how everything going on with ICE is even worse than it looks; Amanda explains how Trump is *de*-legalizing millions of people who thought they were protected; and Doug shatters any remaining illusions that MAGA is okay with legal immigrants.

Plus we introduce ourselves, drag the New York Times a bit, and give you a few things to be hopeful about in 2026. Join us!
